utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good morning to everybody in and around the courtroom. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-81-T, the Prosecutor versus Momcilo Perisic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Could we have the appearances for the day starting with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours, General Nikolic, everybody in and around the courtroom. Carmela Javier, Barney Thomas, and Dan Saxon for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. And for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to all the parties to the proceedings in the courtroom and around it. I would also like to congratulate all the women in the courtroom and around the courtroom because of the International Women's Day. Mr. Perisic will be represented by Novak Lukic, Gregor Guy-Smith, Boris Zorko, and Tina Drolec.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Lukic and particularly for noting the day. And good morning, Mr. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just to remind you that you are still bound by the declaration you made at the beginning of your testimony to tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing else but the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On Friday we left off when we looked at a number of documents. You remember that you analysed some of them. We will deal with some more documents in the course of this morning and then I will complete my examination-in-chief. But let me go back to something that you said, something that you testified. If you recall, we looked at P1872. You don't have to consult your folder. It's the table that was submitted to the Supreme Defence Council on the strength with two categories of people who were in the Republika Srpska army who were already there and those who was seconded there. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, the second category, those who were sent to the SVK and VRS, where were they sent from?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise, but my screen is not working. But I can give you my answer. As you have said yourself, the second category of persons comprised persons who were sent from the territory of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia and were no longer part of the Yugoslav Army chain of command but became part of the chain of command of the Republika Srpska army and the Serbian Krajina army, the SVK.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In this chain of command of the VRS and the SVK, who assigned them to their posts in the establishment?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The assignment and the appointment and all the other issues pertaining to their status in the service was regulated by their superiors, superior officers, in line with their jurisdiction and powers and in line with the laws of the VRS and the SVK.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General, do you know whether the Yugoslav Army, the officers from the Yugoslav Army, have -- did they have any influence on their appointments in the two armies, the VRS, the SVK?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And was it important for the Yugoslav Army or for the authorities of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia that paid the salaries of those persons to know what posts these people had, what rank, and any other categories that are relevant?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your question. I didn't hear you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was it important for the Yugoslav Army and for other authorities of the FRY to know what posts, what ranks, what functions these people held?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And I can give you additional explanations in this regard. This was very important for the following reason. As I have already noted, the salaries of these people were determined on the basis of their rank, post, the military bonus, their length of service, and so on. Any changes in their appointment, for instance, if they were no longer company commanders but became battalion commanders or if they were promoted to a higher rank, it affected their salary, their overall remuneration. And for this reason it was necessary to have this so that they could, in line with the regulations in force at the time, exercise all their rights pertaining to their status.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In line with whose regulations, what country?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Federal Republic of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I would like us to look at Prosecution Exhibit P1523, page 2. [In English] 1523. [Interpretation] Perhaps we could look at page 1 first. I think you have this document in front of you.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please just give me the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: P1523. I think it's an extract from another lengthy Prosecution exhibit. It's an order from the chief of the personnel administration of the General Staff of the Yugoslav Army dated the 15th of February, 1994, affecting a large number of people.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please look at page 2 in the B/C/S, and I believe it's also page 2 in the English version, Bogdan Sladojevic, yes, that's correct, and Milan Celeketic. Yes, we have it in the English version. It says that it's actually the 33rd page of this large comprehensive document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So please look at page 2 where Sladojevic and Celeketic are mentioned. I think it's a good idea to look at this page because we have some typical information listed here?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General, so pursuant to an order of the chief of the personnel administration, as we have seen on the previous page, let me read this out and you can tell me whether this is correct. It is stated that Bogdan Sladojevic is in fact appointed to the General Staff of the Yugoslav Army, the 40th Personnel Centre, 11th Corps; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The first question is: Do you know whether the 11th Corps actually existed in the Yugoslav Army at that time?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From 1970 until the end of my military career in the Yugoslav Army, the 11th Corps was never part of the Yugoslav Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: To the right we have the date, the 10th of November, 1993. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What does this date signify; do you know that?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a date code. This was the date when the president of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, Lilic, issued his order regulating certain issues that pertained to those categories of persons. And it's the order of the 10th of November, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We can see the same date for the other person here on this page, that's Milan Celeketic, here where it says "date," the 10th of November?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. The Belgrade garrison is mentioned here. Perhaps we could scroll down a little bit so that we can compare. We can see here for Milan Celeketic, it's similar to what it says above for Sladojevic. He is assigned to the Yugoslav Army General Staff to the 18th Corps of the 40th Personnel Centre. I have the same question for you: Did the 18th Corps exist in the Yugoslav Army; do you know that?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you one more question. The Belgrade garrison is mentioned as regards to both of these people, and we have two different codes, 683 and 669; do you see that?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know by any chance what is the meaning of those codes; what do those figures or numbers represent?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not the Belgrade garrison. It's the place where the corps command is located. 683, that's for the 11th Corps; and for the 18th Corps, we can see again that it says Belgrade garrison, but the code now is 669. These are in fact locations where the corps command -- corps commands were located.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In what army?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the Army of the Republic of Serbian Krajina, because this is the 40th Personnel Centre. I can add --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let me just ask you one more question. For Sladojevic it says under the peacetime establishment he taught tactics in the school -- in the Petar Drapsin School. We have some abbreviations here. You are probably better placed to understand them. And from the 21st of February, 1993, the Banja Luka garrison. That's what it says. Now, my question is whether you know at the time where this decision was taken, the 10th of November, 1993, do you know if Sladojevic at that time was already in the Serbian Army of Krajina at the post of the commander of the 11th Corps; do you know that by any chance?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my knowledge, he was transferred to the Serbian Krajina army even before this date. And in my opinion this date - the 10th of November, 1993, and you can see that in the code that you mentioned a little while ago, 101193 - and what this means is that the chief of the personnel administration has to and is duty-bound to bring previous orders in line with the order of the president of the FRY of the 10th of November, 1993. And in my opinion, those persons had been seconded or transferred there before, but under the law on the service in the armed forces invoking Article 271 or in some orders 284, indicates that people were transferred even before this date.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a correction for the transcript. At page 6, lines 23/24, the witness said in the Serbian Krajina army, because it says the 40th Personnel Centre. Probably he meant because that's what is written there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, I don't understand you, Mr. Lukic. That's what he said, read it at lines 23. In the Army of Republic of Serbian Krajina, because this is the 40th Personnel Centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, because this is the 40th Personnel Centre -- in first draft, and now it's better because it says -- only a small correction because he read it in the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you want to add something regarding this document, because I have dealt with it. I don't have to explore it any longer. Can we please now look at 65 ter document, it's a Defence document, 00417D. I don't know if you can see the document.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 00417D. Okay. Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, what is this document, who issued it, and pursuant to what regulations?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a decree by the president of the Republic of Serbian Krajina, Milan Martic, on the fast-track promotion of Milan Celeketic, colonel of the SVK. He was fast-tracked to the rank of major, and Article 78, paragraph 1, item 5 is invoked here specifically of the Constitution of the Republic of Serbian Krajina. And -- The microphone appears to be off.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, no, no. It's fine.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Article 46, paragraph 1, Article 153, paragraph 1, item 2 on the Law on Defence, these are laws and regulations of the Serbian Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have an exhibit number for this document, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: This document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, this document shall be assigned Exhibit D257. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 00277D, 65 ter D.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic, 277D for you.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've got that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The header reads Military Post 7572-6, Sarajevo. The preamble reads Military Post 3001 Belgrade, signed by Colonel-General Ratko Mladic. The military post in the header, what army's associated with that?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 3001, that is the 30th Personnel Centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What about the stamp right above, do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the command of the Main Staff of the VRS, at least that's what I think, signed by the commander of the Main Staff of the VRS. That leads me to that conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Where it says "decision," and then on the right-hand side, "verified by controller 4," there is some sort of a date there as well. Who is this controller or supervisor, the stamp that you can see on the right-hand side?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Earlier on in my testimony, I spoke about the way salaries and compensations and benefits were paid, and this was done by the accountancy centre of the federal defence ministry. It appears here that there was a controller who found this document to be accurate and gave the go-ahead for the salaries to be paid, which means in practical terms that this person can now receive his salary under the regulations then in force and applied throughout the VJ.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we pull this up a little just to see who it was addressed to.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At the bottom of this page there is an order to deliver. I see that it's there in the English but not in the Serbian.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was delivered to the accountancy centre of the defence ministry, and a copy was sent to the archives where all of the records were kept. That's DPD 1 and DPD 2, the files we discussed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May this be received, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's admitted, may it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, this document shall be assigned Exhibit D258. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next document is also a Defence 65 ter document, 00141D.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic, that's number 141D for you.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've got it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what it is and who produced this document?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In actual fact, this document confirms what I said a while ago, the service situation for the VRS members and the SVK members. In this specific case, it is a decree by the president of the Republika Srpska on the cessation of professional military service and dismissal from duty of General Novica Simic. If you look closely at this document, you can see that the vice-president, Dragan Cavic, invokes Article 106 of the Constitution of Republika Srpska and Article 115, paragraph 1, item 3 of the Law on the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Actually, I won't be asking this question. May this please be received. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be assigned Exhibit D259. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Another document very much like this one from the Defence 65 ter list. 00368D --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: One speaker at a time, please. We couldn't get the number. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Lukic, the interpreter couldn't get the number because it was not one speaker at a time --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: -- sorry, Mr. Lukic, Mr. Lukic, the interpreter warns precisely against more than one person talking at the same time. Thank you so much. 368D.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've got it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General, what is this document and who produced it?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document was produced by Military Post 7572 Banja Luka, specifically Chief of the General Staff of the VRS, Novica Simic, a lieutenant-general by rank. This is a decision in relation to the dismissal from duty Of Lieutenant-General Bogdan Sladojevic. He's now no longer a professional military serviceman.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: There are several institutions stated as addressees, but what about RS SMO, is that the account centre of the federal defence ministry?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You could see that it was delivered to DPD 1, that is the central archives. There was a receipt. The SOVO fund, military social insurance, and can I explain why?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To make sure that he got all of his pension and disability benefits. The accounting centre for his salaries to be calculated, the unit in which he happened to be, and DPP 2, which is the basic unit, keeping all of the records to do with this person who is the subject of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May this be received, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be assigned Exhibit D260. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this is another Defence 65 ter list document, 00407D.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is from Military Post 9000, the 14th of February, 1995, 9000 is from Knin, and this was sent to 4001 in Belgrade, another military post number.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: First of all, sir, what does this document say? What is this military post code? Which army is that? Who are they sending this to? And finally, why?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right. I apologise. It's a complex question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What is this military post up in the header 9000 from Knin, which army does that code belong to?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 4001, Belgrade, that's the 40th Personnel Centre, and that is the SVK.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just a minute. I wasn't asking about that one. It was actually addressed to 4001, the 40th Personnel Centre, but who is the body dispatching this document or sending it? Who is the sender?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we pull this down, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You see the header up left, military post code. It's got a - wait a minute, please, sir - 9000, and then document number, date, and it says Knin. What army are we looking at here?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 9000, military post of the SVK.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And they are writing to?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 40th Personnel Centre in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we pull this down just a little, please -- or rather, pull it up, up. I said it wrong, down.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: There is a round stamp down there towards the bottom of the document. Which army is that, and who signed the document, sir?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The stamp is from 9000 Knin. And if I may just add something about this document --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: My idea was -- this is my third question - to ask you what the reason is for this military post to be addressing the 40th Personnel Centre, why was this sent?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the beginning of the document, it says that in the attachment they would be forwarding some decisions in relation to professional servicemen. Article 24, paragraph 3, official military gazette, 3893. The decisions were adopted by the authorised officer, and they relate to service in conditions of hardship. If you look at the last part of this document, Colonel Krnjaic is here submitting a request for these decisions to be verified and forwarded to the accounting centre, whereas single copies is to be returned to the Main Staff of the SVK so that it could be filed and archived.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Why are these decisions here forwarded to the accounting centre and just whose accounting centre?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These decisions are forwarded to the accounting centre so that certain salaries and benefits may be calculated and paid.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I asked whose, the defence ministry?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The accounting centre. It doesn't say exactly. It was stated clearly earlier on. The accounting centre of the Ministry of Defence. This accounting centre, as I said earlier on, was subordinated to the administration for the funding and budget of the defence ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May this be received, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be assigned Exhibit D261. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm done with my examination, but I do have a correction to make in the transcript, page 13, lines 9 and 10, when he was reading and then it says -- the witness said that's the 40th Personnel Centre -- I don't wish to be appearing to lead the witness. The 40th Personnel Centre, that is the SVK.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you were reading the document, what exactly did you mean by the "40th Personnel Centre"?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 40th Personnel Centre is attached to the personnel administration of the General Staff of the VJ.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So members of what army are we talking about here in this case?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Members of the SVK.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, General Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this concludes my examination of the present witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Lukic. Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. If I could just have a brief moment to organise myself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: General, good morning. My name is Barney Thomas. I'm a lawyer for the Prosecution. I have the opportunity at this stage in the proceedings to ask you a few questions about the testimony that you have given over the last few days. I ask you, please, to listen carefully to my questions; your answers are important. If you do understand any of my questions, please let me know and I'll ask them for you in a different way. Do we understand each other, sir?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and good morning to you too.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like to start just very briefly with a matter of clarification on a document that we have just been looking at, please, and that is D259.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: If we could have that on the screen.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, I can't see it on the screen. Can I have a hard copy of this document because I can't really see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: General, throughout your cross-examination we will be referring to documents on the screen. They will take a moment or two to appear on the screen, as I call for them. They can always be enlarged, portions of them can be enlarged. So if you counter, as we discuss any documents, any portions which you have difficulty reading, please let me know and I will arrange for a particular portion to be enlarged. All right?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This document -- well, the General has it in his binder. 141D, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can see it on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Now, General, we looked at -- or you looked at a couple of such documents this morning, decrees on the cessation of professional military service, and this one relates to General Simic. What is the effective date of termination of his service?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, according to the text of the decree, we can conclude unequivocally that this person's service is terminated on the 29th of October, 2002.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And we see, General, that the decree itself was issued on 1 November 1992; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Thomas, you said November 1992?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, 2002. My apologies, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the bottom left-hand corner it says number 02-111-775/02. 02, that's the designation of the year, and the location is Banja Luka. The date is the 1st of November, 2002. That means that at that time that this document was logged at the time in that command.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right, General, I will need your assistance here, then, please. Is there anything on the document apart from that logging of the document which assists in determining what day the decree was issued?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Below this number that I read out, in my opinion, because this is the -- a document from Republika Srpska, from the president of the republic, so in my opinion it was logged in the military office. And the internal number is 01-229302, the 1st of November -- well, we can't see the year here, but I think it's 2002 in my opinion. There's no year. It says just the 1st of November.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right, General. Let me ask it this way. Is it fair for us to assume that this decree was issued on or about the 1st of November, 2002?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, sir, but it would not be proper for me to interpret whether this is a document of Republika Srpska, the president of the republic, the military office, the way in which it is logged, and all the rest. Any interpretation on my part would perhaps be less than valid. But I told you what was written here, where it was logged, and who logged it, and when this person's service was terminated. And you can also see where this person was relieved of his duty. And, sir, if you look at this decree, this person was relieved of his duty as of the 11th of November, 2002; and immediately after that, the dismissal followed. The date is the 11th of November, 2002, which means 11 days after the end of the service, the termination of the service. And there was a special procedure for the dismissal. This is what I can read from this decree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, but, Mr. Nikolic, thanks for that long explanation, but it doesn't answer the question put to you. The question is: Is it fair to assume that this document was issued on the 1st of November, 2002? You can either say: Yes, no, or I don't know. Very short answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Nikolic. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, General. And that means that the decree was issued after the agreement on special parallel relations was concluded between the FRY and the Republika Srpska; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, General. I just want to -- I've finished with that document now.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And, General, I just want to go back to some background matters that you spoke about last week. And particularly, sir, I want to discuss the relationship or the workings of the Ministry of Defence of the FRY and the General Staff of the VJ following the restructuring which occurred prior to General Perisic becoming Chief of the General Staff. All right. Do you follow me, sir?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Do you agree, sir, that under the new system the only source of financing for the Army of Yugoslavia was 100 per cent from the federal budget?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Do you mean the funds from the federal budget allocated for the army?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Yes, I do, sir. Did that constitute the universe of funding for the Army of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my answers I stressed in particular that all the funds that the Army of Yugoslavia had at its disposal were obtained through the federal budget and only from the federal budget. That was a joint budget, but it was called the military budget --

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Just pause, please, General. As I indicated to you at the beginning of my questions to you, please listen very carefully to my question, answer only my question. All right? I only asked you if the funding came exclusively from the federal budget. We will move on to those other matters. Please just answer the question I've asked you. Okay?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, this financing or this funding was based on an annual budget; is that right?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not receiving interpretation. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: That process would begin with the General Staff of the VJ preparing a combined plan of all the needs of the VJ for the upcoming period; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: These would include such things as war reserves and salaries as well as all other matters required for the operation of an army; correct?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: By way of additional explanation, you talk about war reserves. I don't know what you mean by that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Well, an army has war reserves, correct, stockpiles and stocks of ammunition and weapons and so on?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And the Yugoslav Army had such stocks?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: For the purposes of preparing the annual budget, they would submit a proposal or they would assess their own needs to either maintain or increase existing war reservist; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And any expenditures considered necessary for that purpose would be included in this plan prepared by the VJ General Staff?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: As would salaries for all VJ officers?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And is it correct that by far the largest expenditure was on salaries for VJ officers?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Can I say approximately how much?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: By all means, sir.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The salaries and pensions took up 60 to 67 per cent of the overall military budget.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: At the stage of drafting a plan for its needs, at the stage of the VJ General Staff drafting this plan for its budgetary needs, the MOD would have no role to play of influence in terms of what it put into its plans, did it?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, but if I may I would like to supplement my answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Certainly, General.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said in my answers that there was an absolute co-ordination in the effort to draft the plan for -- and the draft budget of the army in the Ministry of Defence, but the defence ministry, or rather, the defence minister is the one that makes the decision, the final decision, at that level. The needs of the General Staff of the Yugoslav Army were always presented in larger figures than the --

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Just pause there, General --

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- actual capabilities allowed.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: General, once again my question was directed only towards the preparation of the plan. All right? Your comments are related to the process that followed. Could you please, once again, keep your answers limited to the question that I ask you. All right? We don't want to keep you here longer, sir, than we need to. Once the General Staff of the VJ had prepared its plan, its budgetary plan, it then required the SDC to endorse this plan or approve this plan; correct?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, but I have to give you an additional explanation here. Sir, may I?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You used the term -- you asked whether the Supreme Defence Council approved that plan. No. The budget was approved exclusively by the Federal Assembly at the proposal of the federal government.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: General, before the VJ presented its plan to the MOD for the MOD's input, it first went to the SDC; correct?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Once again, I think there has been a misunderstanding here. May I try and explain?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Yes, by all means.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You keep talking about the Supreme Defence Council. Here we're talking about financial means, the budget, as you stressed yourself. The defence ministry as the line ministry in the federal government is duty-bound to draft the military budgetary plan in co-ordination with the General Staff of the Yugoslav Army, as I have already said. And this plan or draft plan is submitted to the federal government. And later on, the federal government in turn submits the plan or the draft plan for the budget for the current year to the Federal Assembly, which then decides on the budget. It's not the Supreme Defence Council that does that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: General, once again, listen to my question and perhaps I'm not being clear. I'm not suggesting that the SDC approved the budget. What I am suggesting, however, is that the SDC approved the plan created by the General Staff prior to the plan being submitted to the MOD; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the question doesn't seem clear to me. The Supreme Defence Council, in line with its powers, approves the development plan for the army; and if there are any additional funds there, the General Staff will bear that in mind when the budget is being proposed to the federal government.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. And once the plan has been prepared by the General Staff of the VJ, it is provided then at that point to the Ministry of Defence; correct?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Now, on the basis of the plan submitted by the Chief of General Staff of the VJ, the Ministry of Defence would then prepare a draft budget on behalf of the entire MOD for inclusion in the annual budget of the FRY; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And this budget or the MOD component of the budget would effectively be comprised of the needs of the VJ contained in the plan submitted by the General Staff and the needs for the internal workings of the MOD, such as the equipment and salaries necessary for the MOD staff; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Is it a fair assessment that this combined budget, this was effectively made up of 95 per cent funding for the VJ and about 5 per cent funding for the MOD?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a unified draft plan. So -- of the ministry and the army. And this draft plan cannot be submitted to the federal government before it is approved by the defence minister. As regards the second half of your question, what percentage went to the army and what percentage went to the defence ministry, I cannot tell you at this point. But to the best of my knowledge, I think that almost 85 to 90 per cent went to the army, to meet its needs; and the rest went to the defence ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Now, these two budgets put together or these two plans put together, the VJ plan and the MOD plan, were these known as the national defence plan?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me repeat once again. These are not different plans. It's a unified draft plan, which is called the military budget. It's not called the budget of the defence ministry. Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right, General. I think we're losing something in interpretation. Nevertheless, let me approach it from this direction. The combined MOD/VJ plan would then be reviewed by the MOD to determine whether the amounts sought by the VJ, for example, were realistically possible; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Once the MOD had settled on what it considered to be a realistic budget, that proposed budget would be sent to the minister of defence for his approval; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Was it often that the VJ asked for more money than it was possible to give in the opinion of the MOD?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And on these occasions would there be discussions between the General Staff of the VJ and the MOD staff responsible for preparing the joint budget as to what amendments to the budget -- or the VJ plan, rather, could be made; is that right?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But, sir, allow me to provide additional explanation. May I? Thank you. At the beginning of your cross-examination I said that the relevant organisational units of the General Staff co-ordinated their efforts; in this specific case the 5th Administration of the General Staff co-ordinated its efforts with the administration for the funding and budget of the federal defence ministry. And until they are able to agree on the terms, they do not submit the document to the defence minister for his signature. So first they co-ordinate their views, those two institutions. But let me draw your attention to the following: The draft plan of the budget is done on the basis of the guide-lines and the parameters issued by the federal government, and which issues it before the budget plan is actually done.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: General, once the MOD approves this combined budget, it is then submitted by the minister to the federal government for inclusion along with all the other ministerial budgets and to the FRY annual budget; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And ultimately the annual budget is -- or an annual budget is approved by the federal government; correct?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. But allow me to explain, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Please do, sir.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the outset I said the government does not approve the federal budget. The Federal Assembly does. And the Federal Executive Council must square everything with them. The federal government establishes a final budget proposal, which is then submitted to the Federal Assembly for approval.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you, General. Now, once the annual budget is approved, effectively funds are transferred to all the ministries who form part of the annual budget for them to disburse against their own individual plans; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And so, any funds spent by or on behalf of the VJ are credited against that portion of the MOD budget that was agreed with the VJ in accordance with the plan submitted by the Chief of the General Staff, was it not?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. May I additionally explain? The question actually contains several sub-questions. May I explain?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: General, let me ask the question a different way. This might be simpler. The annual budget approved by the Federal Assembly details the expenditures to be made on behalf of each federal ministry; correct?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: In terms of the expenditures to be credited against the Ministry of Defence, the annual budget details what is to be spent on the VJ and what is to be spent on the Ministry of Defence; correct?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: On the basis of that, expenditures are then made; correct?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of that, the defence minister adopts a decision on the expenditures for the VJ and a special decision concerning the organisational units of the defence ministry, meaning he adopts a decision on expenditures.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: In accordance with the annual budget approved by the Federal Assembly; correct?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Now, the VJ for its own ability to function needed funds which it could spend in accordance with that annual budget; correct?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And these funds were transferred to the VJ almost daily to enable it to function; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Specifically they were sent to the accounting centre at the General Staff of the VJ; correct?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The accounting centre calculated and paid out salaries which was a segment of the overall budget. The accounting centre was also in charge of making actual payments to what we called suppliers for the food that was sent to the army, for the beds, for example, and all the other equipment.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: General, pause, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... when a time is convenient.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Now would be an appropriate time, sir. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. We'll take a break and come back at quarter to 11.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: General, would there be occasions when large disbursements on behalf of the VJ, for example, for large construction projects or the purchase of large amounts of ammunition would be made on behalf of the VJ by the MOD?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, Mr. Prosecutor, with all due respect, given the fact that these are questions that exceed my competence, I can hardly be expected to answer questions about logistics, because these are questions to do with the more logistical aspects. Any answer that I might provide concerning issues such as these might be no more than very general answers and not sufficiently valid, I suspect, for the Trial Chamber to take into consideration.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. No, I understand. Nevertheless, you would be able to answer this question for me I think, that it was the army who controlled its own war reserves?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The answer is both yes and no.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Can you explain, sir?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The VJ had control over the equipment and weapons that it was in the actual possession of and whatever it was using. As for whatever the federal defence ministry was using, they were in charge of that, and they were controlling those reserves.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: So the VJ's own war reserves were under the control of the VJ General Staff; correct?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the most part, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: I wonder, Your Honours, if we could please go into private session just for a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in private session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Yes, Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Could we please have Exhibit P1009 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: General, as this document appears, if you would just give it a moment, but when it appears you will see that it is an order issued by President Lilic in 1994 on supplying the 30th and 40th Personnel Centres with weapons and military equipment; you see that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that in the B/C/S document which -- we should have the following page, which what I think is a cover letter.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise. I see a cover letter there on my screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Just pause for a moment, General.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Registrar, do we have the next page in B/C/S? Sorry, page 3. Thank you, and I'm indebted to counsel, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: So, General, again to repeat my question. You see this as an order of President Lilic on supplying the 30th and 40th Personnel Centre with weapons and military equipment. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And you'll see that he orders that it is the Chief of the General Staff who was responsible for reconciling requests with the means of the army to fill them; do you see that?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Based on what it says here, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Would it follow then, General, that this is an order to the supply the 30th and 40th Personnel Centres from the war reserves controlled by the army?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, the order to supply the 30th and 40th Personnel Centres from the war reserves in terms of equipment and weapons is something that never could have happened, for the 30th and 40th Personnel Centres to be in this situation. These units numbered between 10 and 12 men each, maybe enough to fill one or two offices. Imagine there was a rocket system arriving in one of these offices, not feasible. Most probably what they say about these supplies to the 30th Personnel Centre, this is probably a security thing. It says the 30th -- the association here is probably with the Main Staff of the VRS and the Main Staff of the SVK. Again, I was head of the personnel administration, and this unit was part of my administration, the 30th Personnel Centre. It was never the case, never ever, that they received anything, not anything that was made of glass, not any type of equipment, and least of all weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: General, I just want to go on with that topic for a moment --

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: But we can do that in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into open session. Do you still want this document to stay on the screen?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honours, that should come off the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the document please be removed from the screen before we go into open session. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: If we look at document P628, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Now, General, you will see that this is issued by the Chief of the General Staff, General Perisic. And it reminds officers of the army that there are protocols in place for supplying logistics to the 30th and 40th Personnel Centres and that these must be followed. You see that?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see anything in the Serbian. I'm unable to read anything at all. Could I please be served a hard copy -- all right, I can see it now. May I just read through it, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Of course, sir.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've read it. I'm now familiar with the substance of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Plainly, sir, in this context, as you have already observed, the 30th Personnel Centre means the Main Staff of the VRS and the 40th Personnel Centre means the Main Staff of the SVK; is that right?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's at least what I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in private session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Yes, Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, I seek an order for redaction for the question and answers dealing with the description of that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What lines are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: They are lines -- sorry, page 32, line 19, sir to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The end of the page?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May we have that part redacted, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: General, you'll see that, in pages 2 and 3 of the document, that the request is for large amounts of infantry ammunition, for example, 5 million rounds of 7.62-millimetre rounds, we have artillery ammunition, we have anti-aircraft ammunition, and we have oil and fuel. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. You might not be in a position to answer this question, but certainly on the basis of the document this is a request for VJ war reserves; correct? And tell us if you can't answer the question.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, again I must point out the following: This is about logistical support, which exceeds my area of competence. Any answer I might provide would be useless. I can look at a document, see what it talks about; nevertheless, I am certain that there are people who are better placed than I am to answer these questions because they were in this actual line of work. Any answer that I might provide would not be sufficiently valid for evaluation purposes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right, General. Nevertheless, are you able to confirm for us that what we have here are requests direct from the VRS to the VJ General Staff without any involvement, for example, of the MOD? Is that what the document shows?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, as we saw at the outset, this is a 1994 document, unless I'm mistaken. May I please be reminded. This is 1994, right?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Could we please have the top of the document, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The 30th of January, 1994. Sir, Mr. Prosecutor, as you already heard, I was part of the defence ministry chain of command at the time. I was head of the system and status-related issues administration. Our line of work was quite different from what we've been discussing. Again, anything I say -- what I can do for you is read what the document says. Nevertheless, as to the substance, as to the whys and wherefores, again I have to point this out - I have no choice but to say it - this is something that exceeded my competence.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: General, I understand. Let's move to an area you're more familiar with.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: P1873, please. We can move, Your Honours, into open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into open session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Yes, Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Now, the page I'm looking for, Your Honours, in English is ERN 0630-6534. It's a document that was used with General Nikolic on Friday.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: General, you will recognise this document. This was the series of documents that contained the MOD opinion on the need to form the -- or a regime to deal with those who were in the VRS and the SVK from the former JNA and VJ. You recall this series of documents?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: I'd like to go, as I said, Your Honours, please, to doc ID number in the English 653 -- ending 6534 and the corresponding document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. -- I don't understand what you are saying, Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Sir, this was a document used on Friday to identify the particular English page. My learned friend referred to a doc ID number of 6534. This is a document where there are a number of different English translations attached to the single B/C/S document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now, is it part of this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: It is. This is the document that we now have on the screen, sir, it's part of Exhibit P1873.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: General, we won't stay long on this document, but this is the Ministry of Defence opinion regarding the difficulties in how to deal those who were from the VJ or JNA and serving in the VRS and the SVK. The first thing I want to draw your attention to -- in fact, what I want to draw your attention to is the last line in the second paragraph. All right. In fact, if you look at the first paragraph there is a -- if you look at the second paragraph, there is a remark that: "... we believe there are no explicit legal grounds for such an order to deal with the issues raised ..." Do you see that reference at the beginning of paragraph 2?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And particularly we are talking about people who are referred to in paragraph 1, namely -- or the issue as that raised in paragraph 1, which is, regulating the status and dispatch of professional officers, non-commissioned officers, and civilians to the Army of Republika Srpska and the Republic of Serbian Krajina. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: So what is proposed here is a means of dealing with that in the absence of a legal basis; is that right?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, it doesn't say that there is no foundation in the law, but that there is no explicit legal foundation for the regulation of those issues that were raised. What that means is that there is no valid legal foundation.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. A comment I want to refer you to is in the last line of the paragraph where the suggestion that -- the next sentence: "However, there is an apparent need for such a political decision to be made at the highest level of command and control, but it goes without saying that the possible implications that would result from this, especially from an international standpoint, will be assessed." Okay? Now, you alluded to this yesterday and the answer may be obvious, but can you tell us, please, what the possible implications are that are being referred to in that document, especially from an international standpoint. What was it that was concerning the MOD about the implications of this?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When our suggestions were given, since this is a document originating from the system and status issues administration, before a decision is taken, an assessment has to be made of any implications. The implications might in our opinion pertain to the international community, because, at that time, the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia was under the sanctions regime; and in the highest political body and at the highest level of command and control when decisions of this kind were taken, those assessments had to be made.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Well, the MOD would have anticipated that there would have been international repercussions had the international community been aware that soldiers were being dispatched to the SVK and the VRS, wouldn't they?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: The MOD didn't anticipate any problem with that?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. The question is different now. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Okay. You mentioned at some point in your testimony yesterday that reference to the 30th Personnel Centre and 40th Personnel Centre in documents is effectively to keep information secret, is that correct, in some documents?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And depending on the context, these can be euphemisms for the VRS and the SVK; is that right?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: I want to move, please, in the same exhibit to document ID number 0630-6538, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Excuse me, and I do apologise. I was hoping that we could get a translation for the word "euphemism." I understand what you mean by the word, Mr. Thomas, but I'm not sure necessarily some other people here do. So if we could get a translation just for that one particular word "euphemism," we would appreciate it. How is it translated into Serbian?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I miss why it was used.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: The reference, Your Honour, is line 19 at page 38. And obviously, Your Honour, I can't assist my learned friend with his inquiry, but perhaps if Madam Interpreter can do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, I guess --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The Serbian word is "eufemizam."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Can we please have -- oh, we have it on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Now, General, you will recall that these statement of reasons issued by the personnel administration of the VJ General Staff for the proposed draft order on how the structure for dealing with this issue should be implemented. You recall that?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And you'll see there that the General Staff in the first paragraph echo in line 6 of the English - I'm not sure of the corresponding line in your language - but there is a reference to the: "... lack of a legal basis or decision by the responsible SFRY state and military order -- organ, sorry, to temporarily dispatch." You see that?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And at the end of that paragraph we have another reference to the absence of legality. "Up until now, all of this was done in accordance with temporary standpoints of the Chief of General Staff of the VJ, and these standpoints were changed from time to time but without any legal basis and in a semi-legal manner." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Is one of the problems that there is no provision in the law by that time and then in the Law of the VJ permitting the transfer of soldiers - let's start with the obvious - allowing the transfer of soldiers to fight in another nation's army?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, the first part that you read out where the personnel administration is stating its view, that's the personnel administration of the General Staff of the Yugoslav Army -- well, you've said so yourself. I can merely give you my interpretation or I can read out what the chief of the personnel administration said by way of explanation to the Chief of the General Staff --

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Just pause there. Just pause there for a moment, General. The statement of reasons effectively adopts the position of the MOD on this matter, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. Just pause there. The MOD considered that there was no legal basis for the dispatch of soldiers to these two armies or for that regulation of their status in the VJ?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but if you allow me, sir, I would like to explain why I said no. I thought that you had asked me whether this is a document from the personnel administration of the General Staff. I meant this document. And what we did was precisely what you yourself said, our opinion on the draft decision. We were not given the opinion of the personnel administration. It was a draft order that was drafted in the General Staff of the Yugoslav Army. And we, the system and status issues administration -- or rather, the sector for status and system issues gave its views and proposals regarding the draft decision. And this is a statement of reasons provided by the personnel administration of the General Staff, at least that's what I can say based on what I see, because I don't see the -- anything else but what is here on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Well, let's go to P1872.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Now, you'll see here that here is a letter from the Yugoslav Army General Staff forwarding some documents to the Federal Ministry of Defence, dated 8 October 1993. And in the body of the letter we see that the Chief of the General Staff agreed with a proposed amendment to the draft order, and that has been re-drafted for the president of the republic. And as for other objections, the Chief of the General Staff -- I'm sorry, the administration for system and status issues -- I'm sorry, the personnel administration of the General Staff of the VJ presented their position and the -- to the SDC, and included also with this letter is the position taken by the Chief of the General Staff at the SDC. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Could we see where the SDC is referred to on the document?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: It's not, Your Honours, but if we go to page 3 of the document, and that's page 2 in the B/C/S. Your Honours, the ERN number is 063 -- sorry, 0630-6544 to 46.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: You'll see there, General, that this enclosure with the letter records the remarks of the Chief of the General Staff of the VJ made to the SDC, and I think you referred to this document on Friday?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. Do we see in that document that the Chief of the General Staff has adopted also the MOD position; in other words, if you look at paragraph 3, do we see his view that the legal position and personal status of all these persons who stayed behind and those who were dispatched there has not been equally regulated regarding salary and so on. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And again, here, it goes: The position that so far the Yugoslav Army did not have a legal basis in the regulations and there has been no decision issued which would permit the Yugoslav Army General Staff to dispatch these persons out of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. You see that?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Okay. I want to look at the next page in the English, please, and it's in page 3 of the B/C/S, where the Chief of the General Staff refers again to this difficulty --

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Madam Registrar, that should be -- that should be the next page. Sorry, could we scroll up, please -- sorry, the original page that you had, the last one. Thank you. Just there. And the corresponding page. The paragraph I want to look at begins, please, "on the other hand," that is in page 3 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: General, do you see a paragraph which begins: "On the other hand, the crucial fact is that there is no solid legal framework which could not come under attack in possible litigation for dispatching these active servicemen outside of the FRY without their consent." Do you see that there?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: What I want to refer to is the next comment: "Therefore, we must also ensure a high degree of protection of the information regarding these activities, which is very difficult ..." then there's a parenthetical remark, "particularly in relation to the local and foreign public." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Does this echo the same concerns that the MOD had about this process?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in part. But, sir, might I provide an additional explanation?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: By all means.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The law on the Yugoslav Army I think in Article 162 speaks about the data protection in no uncertain terms, especially when it comes to issues such as this one. Any violation would be tantamount to an infraction of military discipline or a violation of military secret or state secret, and such persons would be subject to criminal prosecution. And I still maintain what I said about the implications. So this is because of the data security. Every army has its documents and files that are marked as confidential to a different degree, military secret, confidential, strictly confidential, and state secret.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: But, General, there is an added dimension beyond ordinary military classified documents here. This is a situation where the FRY was anticipating sending people to these two armies without their consent and in violation of Security Council Resolutions to provide assistance -- or to not provide assistance to the Republika Srpska. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I think it's a compound question, sending without their approval and in violation of the Security Council Resolutions, and so on. I think that it should be cut up into several questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: I can deal with that, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: There was an intention to send soldiers or officers to the armies of the VRS and the SVK even without their consent, wasn't there?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Pause. I wanted to go down two paragraphs from what we were reading. And this, again, is the comments of the general -- Chief of the General Staff, General Perisic, to the SDC. "In the proposed Order of the President -- prepared for signing by the president. "In the proposed order of the President of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, and by decision of the Supreme Defence Council, which would become operational and put into effect through the order of the Chief of the General Staff of the Yugoslav Army, this task would be resolved in such a way that all professional officers and civilians serving in the Yugoslav Army who were born in Croatia or Bosnia-Herzegovina and sent to do their training or service in the JNA from these territories, would be obliged to respond to call-up from the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska or the Republic of Serbian Krajina, or else their service in the Yugoslav Army would be terminated. "The relevant officer in the Yugoslav Army would make all these persons available and send them to a special organ of the Yugoslav Army General Staff (personnel administration), based in Belgrade." Now, General, does that not suggest to you that there was an intention to send people, no matter what their position on being dispatched was?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I'm thankful to you for reminding me of those elements that we in our administration for system and status issues highlighted; and when we commented on the order of President Lilic, all of these issues were deleted. They are not there. And the Chief of the General Staff here presents his opinion in these preparatory actions. And in light of the circumstances and the context, the persons that remained there until the 19th of May, 1992, on a voluntary basis, should also include the persons who were in the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia but were born in the territory of Republika Srpska and the Republic of Serbian Krajina and were sent for training from those two republics or to serve in Yugoslavia, that they should respond to the call-up and take part in defending their own people. And since nobody was forced to go, but for the most part as far as I know nobody was forced, nobody was ordered to go without their agreement. If I may draw your attention to this: When I was employed in the personnel administration of the Army of Yugoslavia, we did an analysis and we never came across any information that would indicate that somebody was forced to serve there. And if anyone was made to go there, those people did not suffer any consequences in terms of their service. And if their rights were violated, they could file a legal suit.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. Well, we'll look in a moment at the question of whether anybody was forced to go or not, but before we do so can we look at P731, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that part of a sentence is missing at page 46, line 16. If somebody refused to go, that's what it's missing. And then it goes on to say they did not suffer any consequences.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, what I do see, Mr. Lukic, "and if anyone was made to go there, those people did not suffer any consequences in terms of their service."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness said "if they refused to go," then they wouldn't suffer any consequences.
