utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Yes, Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I just want to deal with that issue now for a moment. Can we please go back to the previous document, P1872, and again the Chief of the General Staff's position which is ERN 0630-6544.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: To 46?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And page 2 in the English and page 4 in the B/C/S -- or the next page in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Now, General, General Perisic has a position on what should happen to those who refuse to go. And I want to scroll down to the last paragraph in the English, please. "For the persons who refuse to be made available and dispatched to the Army of Republika Srpska or the Republic of Serbian Krajina, the relevant officer in the Yugoslav Army would immediately issue a document terminating their service in the Yugoslav Army." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: I wonder if we could please have Exhibit 2827 on the screen. And perhaps, Your Honours, just before that comes, up let me just check that that is not a protected document. It is not. We can deal with it in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Now, General, this is a document --

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you blow this up, please, a little. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Just take your time to read it, General, and then we will put the English version up for Their Honours. And it's probably sufficient for our purposes, General, if you just read that one page so I don't need to go into the second page of the document.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And, Madam Registrar, if we could please have the English version on the screen for Their Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: General, you'll see that this is a document from the 3rd Army command, 3rd Army of the VJ, that is, to the Nis and Pristina Corps commands and to the 1st Anti-Armour Battalion commands, all units in the 3rd Army, following the orders given by the chief of the VJ - and I'll need your assistance here - our translation is "Main Staff," but that should be "General Staff." Correct?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Go ahead, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, there is a request following the orders of the Chief of the General Staff that officers -- that certain steps need to be taken in relation to officers who failed to follow an order on deployment to the 40th Personnel Centre or who otherwise left units of the 30th -- sorry, 40th Personnel Centre of their own will. Now, just -- I understand what you mean about the 40th Personnel Centre being ten people in a small office. What we're talking about here are soldiers who disobeyed an order to deploy to the SVK and those who deserted from SVK units; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before I answer yes or no, these are not soldiers. These are officers. As for the latter part of your question, yes, these are officers who abandoned their units of their own free will without proper authorisation or simply failed to report. The third part of the question that you asked me was the 30th/40th Personnel Centre, these were subordinated to the personnel administration of the General Staff of the VJ. Records were kept there of all soldiers. And obviously all status-related issues as well as any other issues could only be dealt with through these two.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, if we look at the steps that are required to be taken in respect of these people, General, the first is to establish the whereabouts of those deployed; the second is to urgently inform the personnel of the 3rd Army command, whether any of them have since returned to the 40th Personnel Centre main composition - and here we mean the SVK; and to pass on an order, finally, to those who deserted or who refused to obey the deployment order, to pass on the order by the Chief of the VJ General Staff that they are required to report to a meeting with him at a certain time and place. You see that?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And the officers concerned are listed in the balance of that letter?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And I'd like to go now to P1865, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: P1865 is a letter from the 3rd Army command dated October -- 7th of October, 1994, reporting on what happened to these individuals as a result of these steps being taken out, specifically after interviews of those concerned were conducted with officers with the -- sorry, after interviews of those officers were conducted by the Chief of the General Staff of the VJ, General Perisic. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, Mr. Prosecutor, this was back in 1994 when the Chief of the General Staff, at least based on this document, had this conversation. Again, I have to say, I was in the defence ministry. As for the text itself, it's clear, isn't it? What I mean to say is I didn't hear your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. No, that's fair, General. I was giving you the details of the document. I want your -- I want your view now on whether this document shows that there were ramifications for those who refused to obey a transfer order, and I will take you to certain parts of this document and show some passages to you. Under the order the 3rd Army --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I may be jumping to my feet prematurely. Perhaps Mr. Thomas was about to show this document. I think it might be a good idea for the witness to go through the entire page before he answers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: I have no problem with that at all, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: General, please take your time. Read through the entire document. And I'll have some questions about it for you when you're ready.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could we please have this pulled up slightly. Thank you. Is there any more text here to be shown? It's all clear to me. Can I have the question now, sir, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Yes, General. Thank you. The first part of the order lists seven individuals who, after interview with General Perisic, will now report to the 40th Personnel Centre; is that right?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The bottom of the page where these persons are enumerated, their tasks are specified. Sir, Mr. Prosecutor, in order to make this a valid answer, I would need to explain something for the discussion to proceed in the right direction. These persons listed here were not sent anywhere without a proper legal foundation. It was under Article 271 of the law. Everything was done under that article. It was their duty to carry out this order, and they left their post. The Chief of the General Staff, probably pursuant to a request of the commander of the Main Staff of Serbian Krajina, is now asking these persons be tracked down to see what became of them. And that is why the conversation took place. Nevertheless, I am looking at the document in its entirety, and what it says is the conversation was about certain people no longer remaining there, but, rather, their retirement is here being requested and another solution sought in terms of regulating their status within the service. So that is what was being done here. No one's hand is being forced, no one is being punished; on the other hand, each person who left their unit must be made responsible under the rules of the army they belonged to and their own chain of command. Since this is the commander of the Main Staff speaking here, he's seeking assistance in the belief that these persons were here in this area that he specifies. I don't see anything controversial about this, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. Well, let's look at this document a little more. After the number 8 on the front page, we have a paragraph which reads: "All above mentioned professional soldiers have to report to the centre of -- have to report to the centre of the military schools of the Yugoslav Army in Belgrade ... with" --

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. Do you see on the front page where eight soldiers are -- the names of eight soldiers -- sorry, eight officers are listed? The first seven are very clear, then there is a line, a blank line, and then we have officer number 8 right in the centre of the page as you are looking at it now, General.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 8 Macak.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Now, the sentence that I'm looking at immediately follows number 8, all right?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: "All the above mentioned professional soldiers have to report to the centre of the military schools of the Yugoslav Army in the Belgrade garrison with adequate field equipment in order to be sent to units of the 40th Personnel Centre. They have to report on the 15th of October at 0800 hours." All right. You see that?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, some of these men had previously deserted their units. For example, if you look at number 1, Vaso Bosanac deliberately left units of the 40th Personnel Centre. Mr. Keca deliberately left units of the 40th Personnel Centre. Some, however, refused to follow transfer orders such as Sergeant Drinic, first class, on duty in the Pristina Corps did not follow transfer order. Sergeant Pupovac, sergeant first class on duty in the Nis Corps did not follow a transfer order. Sergeant Bogdanovic, sergeant first class on duty in the Nis Corps did not follow a transfer order. And the rest of that list is all in relation to officers who did not follow the transfer order to the 40th Personnel Centre; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: If we go down to where there is reference to warrant officer Mraovic, please. Just take a moment to read that paragraph, and then I'm going to have the English version placed on the screen for Their Honours.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mraovic Ljubana Zeljko, warrant officer first class, on duty in the Nis Corps --

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Just read it to yourself for the moment, General. When you're done --

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Could we have the English on the screen for Their Honours. And, Your Honours, I'm looking at about two-thirds of the way down the page where there is reference to Mraovic and Sakic. Now, in relation to Mraovic and Sakic following their meeting with the Chief of the General Staff, as either individuals who had deserted 40th personnel units or had refused to transfer to the 40th Personnel Centre, the order here is to initiate procedure for the termination of their professional military service, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what the document says, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And if we look, Your Honours, at the next page in English, I think it's the same page in the B/C/S, they are handed one more opportunity.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: "In case that above named do not want to terminate their professional military service upon their request, they are to be referred to report to units of the 40th Personnel Centre in the period regulated by point 1 of this order." So in other words, the only way they could avoid termination was to request transfer to the 40th Personnel Centre; isn't that what the document says?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the text certainly suggests that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right --

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, may I have a minute, please, three minutes, a break for ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Your Honours, now would be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We will take the break. We'll come back at half past 12.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Could we please have Exhibit P731 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And, General, just while that's coming, I hope you're feeling a little better. Please don't hesitate, if you need a break, to do what you did and request one.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Now, General, this was ultimately the order that was signed by President Lilic on the formation of the personnel centres; is that right?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see the entire order, but that should be it.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Perhaps if we just go to the last page, Madam Registrar -- sorry, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. I want to go back, please, to paragraph 1, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right, General, and the first part of paragraph 1, President Lilic identifies the category of person to whom -- or in respect of whom the order is to reply; namely, active duty servicemen, contract servicemen, and civilian employees of the former JNA who remained in the territory of Republika Srpska and Republic of Serbian Krajina and the professional servicemen and civilians employed in the Yugoslav Army who were born in the former republics of Croatia and Bosnia and Herzegovina and were admitted to military schools or joined the JNA for those countries. Am I reading that document that identifies the category of person?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: The second part of that paragraph deals with their dispatch. The individuals mentioned in the previous paragraph shall be: "... dispatched, assigned, transferred, and appointed, depending on the needs of the service and the individuals' abilities, as per the establishment of personnel centres that will be set up by the Chief of the General Staff of the Yugoslav Army."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see that the LiveNote is blocked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We'll wait.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It looks like it's taking a bit of time to get started. We'll take a break, and we'll be called. --- Break taken at 12.41

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thomas -- does it mean the couple of words or the few words that were mentioned between you and the witness are not going to be recovered?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: It looks like it, Your Honour, but I think I can get through that quickly again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If you would. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: General, we're looking at document P731 on the screen and just before we adjourned you were able to confirm that this was ultimately the order signed by President Lilic authorising the formation of the 30th and 40th Personnel Centres?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, in President Lilic's order it is merely stipulated that personnel centres would be established, not specifying which ones, so not the 30th and the 40th Personnel Centres, but just personnel centres.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Now, General, you're quite right, and I should have been more particular with my question. But this is the Lilic order that effectively began that process?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And paragraph 1, the first part of paragraph 1, identifies a particular category of person, namely, active-duty servicemen, contract servicemen, and civilian employees of the former JNA who remained in the territory of Republika Srpska and the Republic of Serbian Krajina and the professional servicemen and civilians employed in the Yugoslav Army who were born on the former republics of Croatia and Bosnia and were admitted to military schools or joined the JNA from these republics.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I did not hear the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: It's coming, General, sorry. I was giving you a moment for your translation. Now, the second part of paragraph 1 states that those people shall be dispatched, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: The only conditions are that this be subject to the needs of the service and the individuals' abilities; is that right?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but we have to add the rest; not only sending, but transfer and appointment to appropriate posts, assignment, transferral, dispatching. You have to list all of those.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: You're entirely correct, General. So these people shall be dispatched, assigned, transferred, and appointed to appropriate posts. What is missing from that paragraph, is it not, is that this dispatch, assignment, transferral, or appointment is at the request of a particular individual? That's not there, is it?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It doesn't say here that this was done exclusively at the request.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Well, General, it doesn't say it's at their request at all.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said - perhaps you didn't hear me right - but I said that it doesn't say, the words are not there, "at their request." And if you allow me, in paragraph 2 there's a reference to paragraph 1, where it is stipulated that the General Staff of the Yugoslav Army shall organise and keep separate records. And then it goes on to list all those things. And in paragraph 2 these people are referred to specifically, or, rather, in paragraph 1, the second passage.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Right, because I want to talk about paragraph numbered 2 now. The second part of paragraph 1 referred to the category of people referred to in the first part of paragraph 1, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. Perhaps -- let me do this a little simply. I asked you a clumsy question, General, and we've already covered this ground. I apologise. The first part of paragraph 1 identifies a certain group of people, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: The second part of paragraph 1 says what is to happen to that category of person, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Paragraph 2 relates to all other people not in that category, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And in respect of other professional servicemen of the Yugoslav Army, the General Staff is under an obligation to enable them to be dispatched, assigned, or transferred, but at their request as well as with the approval of the head of the personnel centre?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, the question that you've just asked me calls for an explanation on my part. These are persons, as you have said yourself, are not listed, there's not an exhaustive list of those people in the first passage of paragraph 1. These are people who want to voluntarily join the VRS or the SVK who are not from the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina or Croatia. And it says here "at their request." This is considered to be their personal request but with the approval of the superior officer from the personnel centre. The reference here is to the personnel centre through which the service status of that person is regulated. And furthermore, as you can see, it is reiterated that they shall be dispatched, assigned, transferred, or appointed to the appropriate personnel centre, echoing what is written in the second passage of paragraph 1. So, again, the same things are valid for those people that we saw in paragraph 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: The difference being the inclusion of those three words "at their request"?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this speaks to the fact that the other people who wanted to join those armies did that on a voluntary basis. If you say "at their request," it means that they did it voluntarily; that's what they wanted. But if you allow me, sir, not a single person, according to what I heard from my predecessor, that was until 1998, did not go to the Republika Srpska army and the SVK without first furnishing a written statement indicating that they accepted the transfer. There were many volunteers from both categories in paragraph 1 and in paragraph 2 who personally requested to go and to join the chain of command of those two armies, the Republika Srpska army and the Serbian Krajina army.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: If somebody in paragraph 2 did not wish to go to either of these two armies, was their service terminated, or did that just apply to those people in paragraph 1 who refused to obey a transfer order?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me say this again. In paragraph 2 we're talking about persons that are not defined in paragraph 1. Nobody's forced to report. If they report that they want to go there voluntarily, their status is regulated as is stipulated in this order. If they don't want to do that, nobody's going to chase them and make them go.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: These are the people in paragraph 2 you're talking about?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two, yes, paragraph 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Okay. I want to look very briefly, General, at paragraph 3. And you will see that the order requires those who were dispatched, assigned, transferred, and appointed from either paragraph, 1 or 2, to carry out their professional duties in accordance with the special work-plan of the personnel centre. Now, I take it that this is not a reference to the work-plan of the personnel centre comprised of 10 or 12 individuals?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 30th or the 40th Personnel Centres had their programme, their tasks, and their purpose. The main purpose was to record and to regulate the service status -- well, it -- it's a reference to those personnel centres. Let me remind you, if you allow me, sir, may I?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Just pause for a moment, General, because I think we're at cross-purposes. The term I want you to focus on is "work-plan" not "personnel centre," all right? Whose work-plan is being referred to in paragraph 3?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me be quite specific. The work-plan of the personnel centres that the Chief of the General Staff would establish later, because in passage 2 of paragraph 1 there's a reference to the personnel centres that will be established, and that's why I asked you to let me explain what this is all about.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right, General, let me ask you this question: Whose work-plan is being contemplated in paragraph 3?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me repeat once again. Later on, the 30th and the 40th Personnel Centres, as they were established later on by the order of the Chief of the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And can you help us with what those work-plans -- what sort of things did those work-plans provide for?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I asked you -- and thank you very much to mention Article 53 on the Law on the Yugoslav Army. The whole of paragraph 3 is not shown here. Could you please show me the next part of this order, because you cannot -- you have to see it in its entirety. You can see that it says here: "Throughout this period, these individuals shall retain all the rights pertaining to their rank and qualification and retain the salary they had in the post they occupied before the current assignment or they shall receive the salary envisaged for the new post, whichever is more favourable ..." You can see in this last sentence "or ... for the new post, whichever is more favourable." So if a person in the VRS or the SVK, pursuant to a special order, was appointed to a higher post, then this post will be taken into account in terms of his status. And that is why the work-plan is defined here. The work-plan is to keep records of all those persons, any changes in their status, any appointments or assignments that occur in the two armies.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. Let me look at this from another direction, General.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Can we please have P2113 on the screen. And if we look at page 2 in both versions, please, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: General, you'll probably be familiar with these sorts of documents. They are -- or this is one of the orders transferring officers to the --

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please zoom in a little bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: This is one of many orders transferring officers to the 30th Personnel Centre. Do you recognise that?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Let's take an example. And there's a well-known one on page 3 of the English and page 3 also of the B/C/S, Dragomir Milosevic. And when you've had a look at the full screen, sir, I'll ask your indulgence for a moment while we put the English version on the screen for Their Honours.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And if we just scroll down a little bit in the English, Mr. Registrar. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: But, General, while Their Honours are looking at this part of the order, can you confirm for me that, by this order, Dragomir Milosevic is transferred and appointed as per service requirements effective 10 November 1993 to the 30th Personnel Centre, specifically command of the infantry corps.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, with all due respect, this order is one in a series of orders that regulate the status and are issued in order to harmonise the earlier set of orders issued before President Lilic issued his order. Look at the right-hand side where it says "date," the 10th of November, 1993. What does it mean? It means that before this date that person had already been dispatched under the Article 217 of the Law on the Armed Forces, and now this is being harmonised in order to ensure that this person may enjoy certain entitlements under the order and a new law.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: General, I'm sorry; you misunderstand me. But it is exactly this order of transfer that is contemplated by President Lilic when he orders that certain individuals be transferred, assigned, appointed to certain posts, the paragraph we were looking at in the previous exhibit, contemplates this kind of order, does it not?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the new order of the president?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Yes. The order we were just looking at --

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: -- authorised the formation of personnel centres and said that certain people would be assigned through these personnel centres, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And so the result of that is first of all we have personnel centres being established and secondly we have orders such as the one that we are looking at right now?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, let me say this once again, sir. Look at the last sentence in this order for this person. "Shall be transferred as of the 10th of November in accordance with the needs of the service when the establishment was defined." So some changes were made, but it was done only to harmonise this with the new order issued by the president of the FRY. And let me just give you an additional explanation. If this order is not harmonised in this manner, this person would not be able to enjoy all the entitles that are guaranteed by President Lilic's order.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: We understand, General. What I'd like to do, please, is go back to P731, paragraph 3.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, paragraph 3 is quite clear to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. Well, we now know that Dragomir Milosevic is transferred by order 5 -- by 75, from memory, to the 30th Personnel Centre. Now, that is contemplated by paragraph 3, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, this applies to both me and you. We both know that the regulations changed. That's why we had those two orders when there were special changes being made to the regulations and a solution was being sought. The day this order was --

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I may, please --

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: No, General, we've spoken about this before. Please listen to my question, answer only my question. There's an order contemplated by paragraph 3, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once again, I can't answer yes or no. I could say both yes and no. Yes in terms of being co-ordinated with this order so that now the new regulations he could exercise his status-related rights. Nevertheless, he was transferred or dispatched, received a transfer under the previous set of regulations, whereas now the new regulations are to be applied. I think I'm being extremely specific in my answer. Can you please go down to paragraph 2 of this? Why exactly is this done?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: General, pause. Let's start this again. I'm looking at the first part of paragraph 3, the first part of which reads: "While performing their duties following the order on dispatch, assignment, transfer, and appointment to a post at a personnel centre ..." My question is this: Is the order we have just looked at an order an dispatch, assignment, transfer, and appointment to a post at a personnel centre?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Pause. Pause. So Dragomir Milosevic has now been transferred and appointed to a post at a personnel centre; and now that he has been so transferred, he needs to perform his duty in accordance with the special work-plan of the personnel centre, doesn't he?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: So what exactly -- again, I come back to my question. General Milosevic would not have been sitting in the personnel centre carrying out status-related financial or accounting duties, would he?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: So whose work-plan?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, Mr. Prosecutor. This is not about carrying out tasks in a unit or an institution in which a person's service situation is regulated. This is about the work programme of personnel centres, meaning record keeping and regulating one's service status. That is the work programme of a personnel centre. It is not something for the Main Staff of the VRS. These are entirely different rules on the use of units, a plan being drawn up for that, and everything else. This is a special programme of a personnel centre, the 30th or the 40th. And paragraph 2 refers to item 3, paragraph 1. Throughout -- or rather, the service situation was regulated there; throughout his time there, he exercises certain rights; and then there's a list of what rights and entitlements. Please bear one thing in mind, this paragraph must be seen within a proper context and not separately.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. General, Dragomir Milosevic would have carried out his duties in accordance with the orders and under the command of the commander of the VRS once he had been appointed to the 30th Personnel Centre?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was not appointed to the personnel centre. He was sent or seconded to the VRS through the 30th Personnel Centre, and that is something that the personnel centre does, and that is part of its programme.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: General, the 30th Personnel Centre was established because there was no authority to send somebody out of the FRY in these circumstances, so the order was to the 30th Personnel Centre because the rationale was that this was garrisoned at Belgrade and therefore within the FRY. We have seen this in the documents that you and I have reviewed already. He was appointed to the 30th Personnel Centre. From there on, he was assigned posts by the commander of the VRS or the Main Staff of the VRS as required; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once again, he was not assigned to the personnel centre. There are no two personnel centres, there is only one -- or rather, two, the 30th and the 40th. But assignments, transfers, secondments, all of this is done through that centre and only ever done by a group of between 10 and 12 men. Any assignments, any regulating service situations or service statuses, is something that superior officers do or whoever outranks him under the laws of Republika Srpska and the Republic of Serbian Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right, General.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Can we see document P2817, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: We'll move on to a different topic of discussion.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Could we zoom in, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Now, General, you spoke last week of a very difficult period and your time at the MOD when the salaries to VJ officers serving in the VRS were stopped, and that was during sanctions imposed on the RS in August 1994 to put pressure on the RS to accept the Contact Group plan. Do you recall that testimony yesterday?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Now, the stopping of salaries caused an enormous problem, did it not, not just for the families who dealt with you but for the servicemen and officers in the VRS?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The very livelihood of the families of persons serving in the VRS and the SVK was at risk. These men themselves were not really facing the same risk in terms of survival or subsistence. Their families were affected more than anyone else, and I was telling you about all the trouble that I was facing because I was the person in charge of sorting all this out, although Article 58 of the --

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. I think we have an answer to my question in there. The --

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: It was important to the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia that the international community understood that the FRY was serious about its sanctions imposed on the Republika Srpska, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: But the stopping of salaries created a very serious problem, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And this problem was ameliorated by contacts between the commander of the VRS, General Mladic, and the Chief of the General Staff, General Perisic. Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was in the system as status-related issues administration. I wasn't at General Staff myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: So at the MOD you were unaware that steps were being taken for money to go from the General Staff of the VJ to the VRS to cover salaries for officers who were members of the VJ? Were you unaware of that at the time?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not aware about the contacts, but I did ask the defence minister, I was one of his subordinates, to use his power and exercise -- exert pressure on the Supreme Defence Council and the prime minister in order to overcome this situation and in order to secure the livelihood of those men's families because they had nowhere to go. If this opportunity was crushed, their very lives would have been at stake.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: No, I think we all understand that, General. Without a salary, a family cannot survive; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Looking at document that is on the screen at the moment --

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, could we zoom in a little, please. I can't see. That's fine now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: We have a -- let us know once you've had the opportunity to read it, sir, and I'll have the English version on the screen put up for Their Honours.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could we please have the header pulled down because I can't read it. And slowly, please. Thank you. It's all right. We can pull it up.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Can we have the English version on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. We can see from the first -- from the heading of the letter or the first paragraph of the letter that it is regarding the abolishment of salaries and the difficulties that this is causing and the fact that these difficulties are causing a situation where attention is unnecessarily drawn from combat tasks, presumably combat tasks of the VRS. Correct?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what the text says.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Now, General Mladic in sending this report to the VRS Main Staff advises that in the last few days - and I'm looking at paragraph number -- numbered paragraph 3 -- sorry, 2 and 3. All right. You can see there that there are meetings with the VJ in order to solve this problem with salaries. You see that?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Paragraph 3, yes. It's misspelled, "janja dana." It's not quite clear what it's supposed to mean. But can you please show me who signed this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: If we could go to the last page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Do you recognise General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but I can't see -- Ratko Mladic, yes, no signature though.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Well, we have it as logged, don't we?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Fine. Can be considered as that. Still, what I'm saying is there's no signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Yes, you're correct, sir. If we go back to numbered paragraph 2 on the previous page, you'll see there that General Mladic refers to meetings with the VJ in order to solve this problem and also a request put in to the Chief of the General Staff of the VJ to solve the salary issue as soon as possible as it was the case with the other VJ members. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I may just correct you, it's not about VJ members, it's about VRS members. Do you think I'm right about that?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Well, I might have a different translation, sir. If you look at the last -- can you read for us in your language what numbered paragraph 3 says?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These "janja." I think what that's supposed to mean is these days. "S-h-o," probably -- probably -- well we did - that's my assumption, I'm sorry - address the General Staff of the VJ with a request to deal with the salary problem in a successful manner. The same as the remaining members of the VJ, so the VJ, my apologies.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. You haven't seen this document before I take it?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No one ever showed me nor was this my document. I was in the defence ministry; I was part of the chain of command of the defence ministry. It's 1994 we're talking about, or rather -- sorry, I think this is the 14th of November, 1994, isn't it, this document? I've never seen this document. But you required that I provide an explanation of the document, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: No. I simply asked you, sir, if you'd seen this document before. And you said you hadn't, and that's fine. I'll move to my next question which is: Do you know why --

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Do you know why General Mladic addressed this concern direct to the Chief of the General Staff of the VJ?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute, please. Because of what the witness read -- I'm looking at the English, I'm looking at the document, and I see General Mladic is here addressing the General Staff of the VJ. There is no mention here of the Chief of the General Staff of the VJ.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Sorry, I'm looking at -- my friend is quite right. My friend is quite right.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Do you know why General Mladic addressed these concerns to the General Staff of the VJ?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In light of the previous answer, I really believe, unfortunately, I have to say Mr. Thomas is asking the witness to speculate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Well, if the General doesn't know, sir, he can tell us. He's testified a lot, sir, on the payment of salaries. I'm simply asking why on this issue of salaries the approach is being made direct to the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: General, can you tell us why General Mladic would be addressing his salary concerns direct to the General Staff of the VJ?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I wasn't there. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Well, we know that as a result of this approach the sum of 500.000 dinar was paid, and I want you to look, please, at document P2770 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I object. The 500.000 dinar document bears an entirely different date and no relation to this one. I think the Prosecutor is now trying to build up a theory about this that simply doesn't hold water. If we display both documents side by side, you will see that the dates don't coincide and in fact don't corroborate what appears to be the Prosecutor's theory.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Would it about your position, Mr. Lukic, that for the documents to be related they must bear the same date? That they couldn't about related even if they were written on different dates?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps we should have the witness leave the courtroom for this discussion so that I could present my argument about this. Nevertheless, it appears to be the OTP's theory that the 500.000 dinar document is a consequence of this document and the talks between General Mladic and the VJ General Staff. I certainly do not wish to testify here, and I'll about offering no further comments, but I believe Mr. Thomas can correspond. It is because of the witness's presence that I do not wish to offer any further comments.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: My learned friend has offered very few comments on the subject, Your Honour. I was going to do no more than put the document to the witness and get him to comment on specific parts. I note the time, Your Honours, that would be a process which, regardless of how we were to proceed, would take some time. I wonder if now would be an appropriate time to stop. We will begin again tomorrow, and I'll begin at the last document that we were at so that if there's any objection, that can be dealt with easily tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I think we must remember tomorrow to begin not at the last document you had but at the fact that there is an objection on the table. We've got to deal with that objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Well, in that case, can I suggest we deal with it now, sir. It will only take a moment to deal with the objection. Unless -- I'll discuss it with my learned friend, sir. We can -- we can -- we might resolve it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We'll take a -- Mr. Nikolic, you are supposed to come back here tomorrow morning at 9.00 in the morning, same courtroom. I still remind you that you may not discuss the case with anybody until you are excused from further testifying. Okay?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. The matter stands adjourned to tomorrow, 9.00 in the morning, Courtroom I. Court adjourned.
